method: Every lead/paragraph sentence group of INST-HOME-EN and INST-HOME-DE classified and checked against the governed stores. Corrections made in this PR: 'A page is published only if…' (contradicted by the legacy corpus) and 'Each reference page names…' (true only for governed pages) were narrowed in both languages.

items.text: A reference project on the language of sulfur chemistry: German and English terms, the compounds they name, and the evidence behind each statement.
items.basis: description of purpose, not a factual claim

items.text: 2 reference records have been built under the current rules so far. The first covers molybdenum disulfide (MoS2): its formula, its layered bulk structure, the 1T, 2H and 3R polytypes, and two independent determinations of the 2H lattice parameter. It rests on 11 admitted evidence records, each traced to the study or database that produced it.
items.basis: fact about the site's own governed objects; counts computed from the registries; descriptions match KO scope fields (KO-MOS2 scope, KO-BISULFID scope)

items.text: 'Bisulfid' and 'bisulfide' differ by one letter. Whether 'Bisulfid' is simply the German spelling of the English term is itself a terminology claim, and it is handled like any other claim on this site: it will be stated as fact only after its sources are verified and admitted.
items.basis: states only that equivalence is an open claim; consistent with Recovery-03 evidence (no claim of equivalence)

items.text: The terminology record sets out, from 15 admitted evidence records and 11 reviewed claims, which meaning dictionaries, IUPAC and a chemical database attach to each spelling, and where the evidence stops. 2 related claims remain open.
items.basis: fact about the site's own governed objects; counts computed from the registries; descriptions match KO scope fields (KO-MOS2 scope, KO-BISULFID scope)

items.section: How a statement reaches a reference page
items.text: A source is first identified and checked, then qualified for a specific use. A passage from it is recorded as evidence with its exact location, and a claim is approved only against admitted evidence. Numbers are quoted as their sources print them; when two determinations differ, both are shown rather than averaged. A new reference page is published only if it adds knowledge that no other page on the site already holds; most older pages were published before these rules and are being reviewed or rebuilt.
items.basis: describes the admission chain enforced by source_admissibility/Contract C; the 'older pages' qualification matches the disposition registry

items.text: The site is maintained in English and German. A German page exists when it answers a German-language question, such as which form a German technical text uses, rather than as a copy of an English page.
items.basis: routes.json: 13,730 en + 270 de routes; no other language published

items.section: Who is responsible for this site
items.text: BISULFID is an independent reference project published by the owner of the bisulfid.com domain. It is not affiliated with IUPAC, with any dictionary publisher or with any company or database named on its pages.
items.basis: publisher = domain owner; non-affiliation with IUPAC/dictionary publishers/companies is an owner statement that cannot be verified from the repository

items.section: Who is responsible for this site
items.text: Each reference page built under these rules names the evidence behind every statement and shows when it was retrieved. No individual expert review is claimed: a page records that it has been independently validated only after such a review has taken place.
items.basis: true today: no signed independent review exists (main/data/release/reviews)

items.section: What you will not find here
items.text: BISULFID does not give safety, handling, medical, procurement or investment guidance. For those, use the safety data sheet of the specific product and a qualified professional.
items.basis: policy statement of the site; matches KO excluded_claim_classes

items.text: ‚Bisulfid‘ und ‚bisulfide‘ unterscheiden sich um einen Buchstaben. Ob ‚Bisulfid‘ einfach die deutsche Schreibung des englischen Wortes ist, ist selbst eine terminologische Aussage. Sie wird hier erst als Tatsache dargestellt, wenn ihre Quellen geprüft und zugelassen sind.

items.text: Die Terminologie-Referenz zeigt anhand von 15 zugelassenen Belegen, welche Bedeutung Wörterbücher, die IUPAC und eine chemische Datenbank der jeweiligen Schreibung zuordnen und wo die Belege enden. 2 weitere Aussagen sind noch offen.

items.section: Wie eine Aussage auf eine Referenzseite gelangt
items.text: Eine Quelle wird zuerst identifiziert und geprüft und dann für einen bestimmten Zweck zugelassen. Eine Passage daraus wird mit ihrer genauen Fundstelle als Beleg erfasst, und eine Aussage wird nur anhand zugelassener Belege freigegeben. Ältere Seiten der Website entstanden vor diesen Regeln und werden überprüft oder neu aufgebaut. Zahlen werden so wiedergegeben, wie die Quelle sie druckt; weichen zwei Bestimmungen voneinander ab, werden beide gezeigt und nicht gemittelt.
items.basis: describes the admission chain enforced by source_admissibility/Contract C; the 'older pages' qualification matches the disposition registry

items.text: Eine deutsche Seite entsteht, wenn sie eine deutschsprachige Frage beantwortet, etwa welche Form ein deutscher Fachtext verwendet, und nicht als Kopie einer englischen Seite. Deshalb sind manche Referenzen vorerst nur auf Englisch verfügbar.
